title: Foundations of Computer Science
description: Discrete structures for computer science: propositional logic, quantifiers and inference; sets, functions and sequences; algorithms and the growth of functions; number theory and classical ciphers; mathematical induction and recursion; counting and recurrence relations; and relations and graphs. Built from the CSC 242 lecture slides (Discrete Structures), the course's logic, algorithms, recursion and cryptography lectures, and Epp's Discrete Mathematics with Applications, which is filed with the course. Also offered as CSC 241.

topics.title: Propositional Logic, Quantifiers and Inference
topics.summary: A proposition is a statement that is either true or false, combined with logical operators into compound propositions whose truth is shown by truth tables. Predicates with the universal and existential quantifiers express statements about all or some objects.
subtopics: Logical operators: negation, conjunction, disjunction, XOR, implication, biconditional
Logical equivalence and De Morgan's laws
Universal and existential quantifiers and counterexamples

topics.title: Sets, Functions and Sequences
topics.summary: A set is an unordered collection of distinct elements, combined by union, intersection, difference and complement. A function assigns each element of its domain exactly one element of the codomain; it may be one-to-one, onto or a bijection, and a sequence is a function on the natural numbers.
subtopics: Subsets, power sets, cardinality and Cartesian products
One-to-one, onto and bijections; inverse and composition
Floor and ceiling functions; sequences and summations

topics.title: Algorithms and the Growth of Functions
topics.summary: An algorithm is a finite set of precise instructions for solving a problem, with input, output, definiteness, correctness, finiteness, effectiveness and generality. Searching algorithms such as linear and binary search are compared by how their time complexity grows, described with big-O notation.
subtopics: Pseudocode: maximum element and linear search

topics.title: Number Theory and Cryptography
topics.summary: Number theory studies divisibility, primes, greatest common divisors and congruences, with the Euclidean algorithm for gcd. It underpins cryptography, from Caesar's shift cipher to affine and transposition ciphers.
subtopics: Greatest common divisor, relatively prime and LCM
Caesar, shift and affine ciphers; cryptanalysis

topics.title: Mathematical Induction and Recursion
topics.summary: Mathematical induction proves a statement P(n) for all positive integers by a basis step and an inductive step. Recursion defines sequences, functions, sets and algorithms in terms of themselves, as in the factorial, Fibonacci and recursive Euclidean algorithm.

topics.title: Counting and Recurrence Relations
topics.summary: Counting uses the sum and product rules, inclusion-exclusion, the pigeonhole principle, permutations and combinations. A recurrence relation defines a sequence by earlier terms; linear homogeneous recurrences can be solved systematically.
subtopics: The pigeonhole principle and its generalisation
Recurrence relations and linear homogeneous recurrences

topics.title: Relations and Graphs
topics.summary: A binary relation from A to B is a subset of A × B; a relation on a set may be reflexive, symmetric and transitive, and an equivalence relation partitions the set into equivalence classes. A graph has vertices and edges; simple, complete and directed graphs are described by degrees and adjacency.
subtopics: Graphs: vertices, edges, loops and parallel edges
